prerequisites: Basic knowledge of digital techniques and digital communication.

learning_outcomes.text: You can outline the structure of a PLC, the master on an industrial network, and list the most important practical differences from a microprocessor (-controller) board.
You can describe its specific operation.
You can describe the most common fieldbuses (where applied, supporting manufacturers, specific use, ...).
You can describe the specific concepts, properties, and terminology used in industrial networks.

For the covered networks, you can describe/display/draw the following: network interface (connectors, cables, signals, specific necessary components), network structure (possible network topologies), operation of the communication protocol, limitations of the network (length, speed, number of components), compatibility with Ethernet TCP/IP.
You can design a PLC program with the most important basic instructions.
You can configure a Profibus and Profinet network in STEP7.
You can commission a Profibus and Profinet network.
You can diagnose Profibus and Profinet networks, both via HW configuration and via a self-written program.

syllabus_topics: Topology and components of an industrial network
Configuration and programming model of an S7-300-PLC (Siemens).
Creating a simple program (with the most important basic instructions).
Setting up a Profibus network with a Siemens-PLC as master.
Setting up a Profinet network with a Siemens-PLC as I/O controller.
Applying diagnostics to a (failing) network, via HW configuration and via a self-designed program.

assessment_methods.method: Theory exam during the examination period
Lab test during the semester (continuous assessment)

assessment_rules: The overall grade for the course is composed of a theory exam (60%) and a lab test (40%). The theory exam includes multiple-choice questions (no guessing correction) and open questions. The lab test assesses the ability to configure and commission a Siemens-PLC, create a simple STEP7 program, and configure, commission, and diagnose a Profibus or Profinet network. If a student scores less than 8 out of 20 on either assessment activity, the maximum overall grade for the course will be 9 out of 20. Resits for the theory and lab components will be similar to the first attempt. Partial transfers of successful module results (Theory, Lab) are possible within and across academic years, but for the overall course to be passed, both components must achieve at least a tolerable grade, otherwise, the final result is max 9/20.
